record.original_question: Let λ be a complex number and let x be a {0,1}-valued pattern Sturmian sequence. For the discrete Schrödinger operator H on l^2(Z) defined by [Hψ](m)=ψ(m+1)+ψ(m-1)+λ x_m ψ(m), must the spectrum σ(H) be a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero, and must all spectral measures be singular continuous?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.1.1. Let λ ∈ C and let x ∈ {0, 1}^Z be a Sturmian sequence. Denote by H the Schrödinger operator defined in the space l2 (Z) as follows : given ψ ∈ l2 (Z) and m ∈ Z, let [Hψ] (m) := ψ(m + 1) + ψ(m − 1) + λ · xm · ψ(m). Then, the spectrum σ(H) of the operator H is a zero Lebesgue measure Cantor set. Furthermore, all spectral measures are singular continuous.
Conjecture 2.1.1. Theorem 2.1.1 holds if x is a pattern Sturmian sequence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{A}=\{0,1\}$ and let $x=(x_m)_{m\in\mathbb{Z}}\in\mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{Z}}$. For a finite window length $n\ge 1$, define the set of patterns of length $n$ appearing in $x$ as
$$L_n(x)=\{(x_{m+1},x_{m+2},\dots,x_{m+n}) : m\in\mathbb{Z}\}\subset\mathcal{A}^n.$$
More generally, for a finite set $S=\{s_1<s_2<\dots<s_n\}\subset\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, define the $S$-pattern complexity of $x$ by
$$p_x^*(S)=\#\{(x_{m+s_1},x_{m+s_2},\dots,x_{m+s_n}) : m\in\mathbb{Z}\}.$$
Define
$$p_x^*(n)=\max\{p_x^*(S) : S\subset\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},\ \#S=n\}.$$
The sequence $x$ is called pattern Sturmian if $p_x^*(n)=n+1$ for every $n\ge 1$. (In particular every Sturmian sequence is pattern Sturmian, but the class of pattern Sturmian sequences is strictly larger.)

For $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$, let $H=H_{\lambda,x}$ be the discrete Schrödinger operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$ defined by
$$(H\psi)(m)=\psi(m+1)+\psi(m-1)+\lambda\, x_m\,\psi(m),\qquad m\in\mathbb{Z},\ \psi\in\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}).$$

Question. Suppose $x\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ is a pattern Sturmian sequence and $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$. Is the spectrum $\sigma(H)$ necessarily a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero, and are all spectral measures of $H$ necessarily singular continuous?
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous statement for ordinary Sturmian sequences (Cantor spectrum of zero Lebesgue measure with purely singular continuous spectral measures) is a classical theorem. The extension to the broader class of pattern Sturmian sequences appears as an open conjecture; web search did not surface a published proof or counterexample establishing or refuting it.

status_evidence.title: Uniform spectral properties of one-dimensional quasicrystals, IV. Quasi-Sturmian potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Operators with quasi-Sturmian potentials are shown to have purely singular continuous spectrum supported on a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the Cantor / singular continuous result for the Sturmian / quasi-Sturmian case, but not for the wider pattern Sturmian class.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on spectral properties of Schrödinger operators with low-complexity potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that extensions beyond the Sturmian setting remain open conjectures.
